# Was the Atlassian Bitbucket and login outage on Nov 23 a hack?

**Not established.** Not established. Atlassian says it found the cause and applied a fix, and services are recovering, but it has not said what the cause is. No one has claimed an attack and we found no report calling it one; no source has ruled one out.

Incident: Atlassian Bitbucket and login outage, Nov 23, 2026. Also reported as the Bitbucket outage and the Atlassian login outage. First published Nov 23, 2026; last updated Nov 23, 2026, 12:37 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Atlassian, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 23, 2026, 12:37 PM ET: **Atlassian has applied a fix and says services are recovering; the sign-in outage also hit Jira and Trello.** Hourly check. Atlassian moved the incident to monitoring at 11:33 AM ET (mitigation applied, signs of recovery), repeated at 11:57 AM ET; not resolved at 12:36 PM ET. The same incident is on the Jira (from 10:19 AM), Jira Service Management, Trello and Developer status pages (from 11:08 AM); Confluence and the main status hub show none. Added 5 sources (4 Tier 1, 1 Tier 3) and claims c010 and c011 (both Confirmed); updated c001, c002, c003, c005, c007, q001, q003, q004 and the head. No cause stated, no claim of responsibility; main question stays Not established. Staleness and privacy checks done.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Large. Potential reach is broad: the failing sign-in service is shared by Bitbucket, Jira, Jira Service Management and Trello, which are widely used by software and business teams. Atlassian lists only partial outages, applied a fix about 75 minutes in, and has not said how many customers were hit.
- Who is affected: People and teams who sign in to Bitbucket, Jira, Jira Service Management or Trello through Atlassian's OAuth service, or run Bitbucket Pipelines, from 10:19 AM ET on Monday, Nov 23. Atlassian reported signs of recovery from 11:33 AM ET; the incident was not marked resolved at our last check.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 10:19 AM | Incident opened (ET) | Per Atlassian's status page |
| 2 | Components in partial outage | Authentication and Pipelines |
| 11:33 AM | Mitigation applied (ET) | Per Atlassian's status page |

### Known so far

- Atlassian's Bitbucket status page opened an incident at 10:19 AM ET on Nov 23 for failing OAuth token requests, and it was still open at 12:36 PM ET.
- On Bitbucket, Authentication and user management and Pipelines are listed as partial outages; the website, API and Git access show operational.
- The same sign-in incident is posted on Atlassian's Jira, Jira Service Management, Trello and Developer status pages.
- Atlassian says it identified the cause at 11:08 AM ET and applied a mitigation at 11:33 AM ET, with signs of recovery. It has not said what the cause is.

### Not known yet

- What caused the outage. Atlassian has not said.
- Whether it was an attack. No one has claimed one and Atlassian has not addressed it.
- How many customers were affected.
- When it will be marked fully resolved. Atlassian was still monitoring recovery at our last check.
